items.descriptionAdvanced: The Aghlabid Basins are monumental water reservoirs built in the 9th century, which ensured the water supply of Kairouan during the Aghlabid dynasty. Representing the peak of engineering science of the time, the basins collected rainwater from nearby hills through a complex system, allowing for the supply of the population and agriculture in a desert environment. The basins, which can still be admired today, are remarkable reminders of early Islamic engineering design and water management, and they continue to be a part of Kairouan's historical landscapes.
factsAdvanced: Water reservoirs were completed in the 9th century, around 862 AD.
Ensured water supply for Kairouan for centuries.
Basins represent the peak achievements of early Islamic hydraulic engineering.
Was one of the most important utility developments of the Aghlabid dynasty.
Basins feature a complex water collection system.
One of the most important historical and engineering monuments in Kairouan.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Trajan's Bridge near Medjez el-Bab is a spectacular monument to Roman engineering precision, built at the intersection of the Medjerda River. The stone bridge raised in 112 AD was an integral part of the vast Roman road network in North Africa, ensuring the smooth crossing of commercial and military troops. Although today only the remains of the massive pillars can be seen, the dimensions and structure of the construction bear witness to the significant investments the Roman Empire made for the infrastructure development of the province.
factsAdvanced: Bridge was built in 112 AD, during the reign of Emperor Trajan.
Served to cross the Medjerda River.
Was one of the strategic points of the Roman road network in North Africa.
Is a remarkable example of Roman engineering knowledge to this day.
Construction demonstrates the ancient economic importance of the region.
Today, the remains of the bridge are considered an important archaeological monument.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Dar Hussein is one of the most prestigious historical palaces in the medina of Tunis, whose roots date back to the 11th century. In its heyday, the palace served as a residence for princes, governors, and high-ranking ministers, being continuously expanded and enriched over the centuries. Today, the building houses the National Institute of Heritage, thus, on one hand, it fulfills an official function, and on the other, it serves to conserve and research the palace's architectural values in the central administrative district of Tunis.
factsAdvanced: History of the palace began in the 11th century.
In its prime, it was the residence of governors and ministers.
Today, it is the headquarters of the National Institute of Heritage.
Prominent example of the medina's architectural heritage.
Its complex current form was shaped over the centuries.
Plays an important role in protecting national heritage.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Kasbah of Bizerte is a historic Byzantine fortress that guarded the entrance to the maritime canal at a strategically important point near the city's old port. The massive walls and bastions of the fort are based on original Byzantine foundations raised in the 6th century, which were later reinforced and developed by the Ottomans to meet new military challenges. The facility is today one of the city's historical prides, representing the long history of the maritime past and defensive capabilities of Bizerte to visitors.
factsAdvanced: Byzantine foundations of the fortress date back to the 6th century.
Ottomans expanded it significantly in subsequent centuries.
Served for strategic control of the maritime canal.
One of the most important historic defensive monuments of the Bizerte port.
Walls combine construction techniques from different eras.
Visible element of the historical landscape of the city.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Dar Jellouli is a traditional 17th-century building in the old city of Sfax, which displays the sophistication and ornamentation of the bourgeois architecture of the era. The palace's rich interior décor, including Andalusian-style tiles and detailed wood carvings, prove the well-being and artistic refinement of the owners of the time. Today it functions as the Regional Museum of Art and Popular Traditions, where visitors can obtain a perspective on the history of the social and cultural life of the city and the region.
factsAdvanced: Dar Jellouli was built in the 17th century.
Functions today as a regional museum of art and ethnography.
Tiles with Andalusian influence are one of the palace's most beautiful decorations.
Wood carvings are remarkable examples of the era's artisanal mastery.
Historical representative of the social and cultural life in Sfax.
One of the most important museum buildings of the city.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The City Hall of Sfax (Hôtel de Ville) is one of the city's most distinctive buildings, bearing the architectural style of the early period of the French protectorate. The building constructed in neo-Moorish style was the representative urban center of the era, with its elegant facade and central tower. The City Hall, situated near the historic city wall, exemplifies the administrative ambitions of then and the architectural current that wanted to combine Western modernity with local traditions.
factsAdvanced: City hall was built in the early years of the French protectorate.
Characterized by architectural solutions in neo-Moorish style.
Central tower is the most important visual element of the building.
Situated in the immediate vicinity of the historic city wall of Sfax.
Building was the center of the urban administration of the era.
Architecturally, shows the mixture of Western and local styles.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Olympic Stadium of Sousse is one of the prominent sporting facilities of Tunisia, known as the home of one of the most successful football teams in the country, Étoile Sportive du Sahel. The stadium inaugurated in 1973 was expanded to host 40,000 people during the last modernization works, thus ensuring the standard corresponding to international regulations. The facility is not only an important place for sports fans, but also a decisive and community-building point for urban life in Sousse.
factsAdvanced: Stadium was inaugurated for the sporting public in 1973.
Home of the famous club Étoile Sportive du Sahel.
After recent renovations, it is capable of hosting 40,000 spectators.
Important venue for Tunisian national football.
Stadium has modern comfort facilities.
One of the city's most important community and sports facilities.
